book.title: A Christmas Carol · Stave 5 — The End of It
book.author: Charles Dickens, A Christmas Carol (1843)

iconic_quotes_kept: Scrooge was better than his word

cast.name: Scrooge
cast.role: the redeemed miser, now warm and joyful
cast.canonical: a thin bent elderly man, completely bald on top with wispy grey side-hair, a long smooth clean-shaven face and a sharp pointed nose, now bright-eyed and beaming with joy, in a dark Victorian tailcoat
cast.anchor: thin bent bald clean-shaven old man, sharp pointed nose, now smiling warmly
cast.distinct_from: the same old bald Scrooge — but now happy, not sour

cast.name: Bob Cratchit
cast.canonical: a thin gentle clerk with dark hair and a mild kind face, wound in a long white knitted comforter scarf, in a threadbare coat
cast.anchor: thin dark-haired clerk, long white comforter scarf
cast.distinct_from: a grown thin clerk — not bald

cast.name: Fred
cast.canonical: a cheerful handsome young man with dark side-whiskers and a small moustache, bright warm eyes, a scarf and a sprig of holly pinned to his coat
cast.anchor: cheerful young man, dark side-whiskers, holly sprig on his coat
cast.distinct_from: young and warm — not the old man

cast.name: Tiny Tim
cast.role: Bob's frail, sweet son — who lives
cast.canonical: a small frail boy with a thin pale face and a sweet happy smile, one leg in an iron brace, leaning on a little wooden crutch, dressed poorly but neatly
cast.anchor: tiny frail boy, iron leg-brace, little wooden crutch, happy smile
cast.distinct_from: a tiny disabled child with a crutch — the smallest figure

panels.scene: the bald pointed-nosed old man in a striped nightshirt and nightcap sitting up in his four-poster bed on a bright snowy Christmas morning, both arms flung wide, his whole face lit with joy and relief

teen.narration: CHRISTMAS MORNING! SCROOGE WOKE — ALIVE, AND FREE.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: I'm as light as a feather, as happy as an angel! A merry Christmas to everybody!

panels.scene: the bald old man in his nightshirt and nightcap laughing and half-dancing in the middle of his plain bedroom, giddy with happiness, tears of joy on his cheeks

teen.narration: HE LAUGHED AND CRIED AT ONCE.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: I don't even know how long I was among the Spirits — but the whole night, and it's not too late!

panels.scene: the bald old man in his nightcap leaning far out of his upstairs window into the cold sunny morning, calling down cheerfully to the snowy street below
a small ragged Victorian boy standing in the snowy street below, looking up in surprise, one hand shading his eyes

teen.narration: THE BOY STARED UP IN SURPRISE.

panels.scene: the delighted bald old man at his window, clapping his hands, calling an eager order down to the boy in the street

teen.narration: HE HAD NOT MISSED IT! THE SPIRITS DID IT ALL IN ONE NIGHT.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: Go and buy the prize turkey in the shop window — the big one! Come back with the man and I'll give you a shilling!

panels.scene: a delivery man staggering to a townhouse door under an enormous plucked Christmas turkey almost as big as himself, in a snowy Victorian street

teen.narration: HE SENT THE GREAT TURKEY TO THE CRATCHITS — WITHOUT SIGNING HIS NAME.

bubbles.text: It was twice the size of little Tiny Tim!

panels.scene: the bald pointed-nosed old man now dressed in his best dark Victorian tailcoat and top hat, out in the snowy street, beaming and tipping his hat warmly to passers-by

teen.narration: HE DRESSED IN HIS BEST AND WENT OUT, BEAMING AT EVERYONE.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: A merry Christmas to you, sir! And a happy new year!

panels.scene: the old man in his tailcoat and top hat shaking hands warmly with a portly charity gentleman on the street, pressing a generous gift on him, both moved

teen.narration: HE FOUND THE CHARITY MAN HE HAD ONCE TURNED AWAY.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: Put me down for this much — and forgive my past unkindness. You are very good!

panels.scene: the old man in his tailcoat standing hopeful and a little nervous at a cheerful front door, hat held in both hands

teen.narration: THEN HE DID SOMETHING HE HAD NEVER DARED.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: Fred! It's your uncle Scrooge. I've come to dinner — will you let me in?

panels.scene: the cheerful young man with dark side-whiskers and a holly sprig throwing the door wide with both arms, his face bursting with delight and welcome

teen.narration: FRED WELCOMED HIM WITH HIS WHOLE HEART.

bubbles.speaker: FRED
bubbles.text: Why, bless my soul — Uncle! Of course! Come in, come in!

panels.scene: a warm bright Victorian parlour full of happy guests at a Christmas dinner, an old bald clean-shaven man in a tailcoat seated joyfully among them, glasses raised

teen.narration: IT WAS A WONDERFUL PARTY. SCROOGE HAD NEVER BEEN SO HAPPY.

bubbles.text: He stayed the whole evening — and felt, at last, that he was home.

panels.scene: the bald pointed-nosed old man in his tailcoat sitting behind his counting-house desk early in the morning, pretending to scowl fiercely, though a smile is breaking through

teen.narration: NEXT MORNING SCROOGE CAME EARLY, TO PLAY A TRICK ON BOB.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: What do you mean by coming in at THIS time of day?!

panels.scene: the thin dark-haired clerk in his long white comforter scarf creeping guiltily to his high stool, trembling, expecting to be dismissed

teen.narration: POOR BOB HAD COME EIGHTEEN MINUTES LATE.

bubbles.speaker: BOB
bubbles.text: I'm very sorry, sir. It shall not happen again — I was celebrating a little too much yesterday.

panels.scene: the beaming bald old man springing up and clapping his astonished clerk warmly on the shoulder, both of them lit with surprise and delight

teen.narration: THEN SCROOGE COULD HOLD IT IN NO LONGER.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: And therefore — I am about to RAISE your salary!
For a moment Bob thought his master had gone mad.

panels.scene: the warm old man grasping his clerk's hand in both of his, earnest and kind, promising help; the clerk overwhelmed with gratitude
panels.composition: close — a promise to the family

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: A merry Christmas, Bob! I will help your struggling family, my good fellow — this very afternoon!

panels.scene: the small frail happy boy with his little crutch and iron leg-brace, alive and well, sitting on the knee of the beaming old bald man who has become like a father to him, a warm fireside behind

teen.narration: TINY TIM DID NOT DIE. SCROOGE BECAME A SECOND FATHER TO HIM.

bubbles.text: Scrooge was better than his word — he did it all, and infinitely more.

panels.scene: a close warm view of the small frail boy with his crutch, his sweet face lifted, glowing with happiness by the firelight
the beaming old bald man in his tailcoat walking a snowy Christmas street among warm, happy people who greet him gladly, holly and lit windows all around

teen.narration: SCROOGE KEPT CHRISTMAS WELL — AND KNEW HOW, IF ANY MAN ALIVE.

bubbles.text: May that be truly said of us, and all of us. And so — a merry Christmas to everyone!
